subject: Acme POC: success criteria & integration plan
messages:
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jordan.pratt@acme.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: POC success criteria and high-level plan

Hi Jordan (and Sasha),

Thanks again for the demo and the discussion earlier — great alignment on the main goals. I promised a short summary of the proposed POC scope, success criteria, and next steps so your team can review internally. Attached is a one-tab workbook (POC-success-criteria.xlsx) that captures the items below.

Summary (proposed POC - 3 weeks):
- Objective: Validate Redwood's Dedicated inference for Acme's customer support summarization pipeline (latency, cost, and quality).
- Duration: 3 weeks of hands-on integration + 1 week for evaluation/reporting.
- Key success criteria (initial):
  - Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency < 350ms for 1k token context under expected traffic profile.
  - Cost: Per-1000-token unit cost within 15% of your internal target (we'll provide detailed cost model).
  - Quality: Summaries meet your rubric: average ROUGE-L >= 0.62 and no more than 5% of outputs with hallucinations per your sample prompts.
  - Reliability: No more than 2% error rate on inference calls over 24h window.

Integration scope / ownership:
- Acme: instrumented test suite, sample dataset, access control review, and primary engineering owner (Sasha) for SDK work.
- Redwood: solutions engineering support (Dev Patel), sandbox Dedicated instance, access to model variants and streaming examples.

Technical highlights we plan to validate during the POC:
- SDK integration (Python/Node) + example API routes for sync and streaming generation.
- Prefix/KV caching configuration to preserve low latency for repeated contexts.
- Tool-calling example for metadata enrichment (webhook + structured tool output).

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- Week 0 (this week): sign-off on success criteria and NDA addendum; exchange test data and env access.
- Week 1: SDK integration + basic sync calls; verify auth and connectivity.
- Week 2: Enable streaming, caching and tool-calling path; run load tests.
- Week 3: Run evaluation, collect metrics, review with stakeholders.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Can Sasha confirm engineering availability and preferred start week?
2) Dev, can you prepare the integration checklist and sample streaming snippet for their team to try (I'll share links)?
3) Jordan, if you agree with the criteria, I'll send a calendar invite for a kickoff meeting and loop in Legal for the minor addendum.

Thanks — excited to get this rolling.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Redwood integration plan + SDK examples (draft)

Hi Sasha, Jordan —

Nice to meet you virtually. Per Marissa's summary, here's a concise integration plan and the key implementation notes for your engineers. I'll be the primary SE for this POC and will host a technical kickoff the first day. Attachment: integration-checklist.pdf

1) Authentication & sandbox access
- We'll provide a Dedicated sandbox token scoped to your env. Token will be delivered via secure shared link.

2) SDKs & API routes (recommended):
- Python SDK (recommended for ingestion pipeline): pip install redwood-inference
  - Example sync call:
    from redwood import Client
    client = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
    resp = client.generate(model="redwood-large-v1", prompt=prompt, max_tokens=512)

- Node SDK (for service endpoints): npm i @redwood/inference
  - Example streaming route (express):
    app.post('/api/summarize', async (req, res) => {
      const stream = client.stream({ model: 'redwood-large-v1', prompt: req.body.prompt });
      stream.on('data', chunk => res.write(chunk));
      stream.on('end', () => res.end());
    });

- Direct REST option (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.company/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","prompt":"...","max_tokens":512}'

3) Streaming considerations
- Use the streaming endpoint for long-context summaries to reduce perceived latency. We'll provide a sample reconnect strategy and binary-chunk handling in the checklist.

4) Tool calling / structured enrichment
- Pattern: call redwood tool that returns a JSON payload with normalized entities, then pipe into the summarizer.
- Example pseudo-flow: ingestion -> entity_normalizer (your service) -> tool-call to Redwood for structured augmentation -> final generate call with tool outputs included as context.

5) Caching & batching
- We'll enable prefix KV caching for repeated conversational contexts to hit latency targets. For batch inference, we'll share batching config that balances throughput and tail latency.

6) Test plan & metrics to collect
- Required telemetry: request_id, model_variant, latency_ms (p50/p95), token_count, error_code, success_flag, quality_score (ROUGE-L/human-eval).
- We'll provide a small evaluation harness you can run (python script).

7) Next steps and kickoff
- Action items:
  - Sasha: share 100 labeled samples + point-of-contact for engineering by Aug 12.
  - Acme: confirm start week (Aug 17).
  - Redwood (Dev): deliver sandbox token and integration-checklist.pdf by Aug 14.

Happy to jump on a technical call — I can host a 60-minute kickoff on Aug 17 if that works.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
